operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are mixed-case (Device_ID, Shop_Name, Package_Version); must be double-quoted in generated SQL.
Tiny tables: device=6, shop=12, stock=8 rows; original_values fully read, no sampling needed.
Open_Date is TEXT storing 'D Month' (e.g. '1 January', '15 July') — no year, no zero-padding; String fuzzer will not reproduce this format.
Open_Year is INT but semantically a year (2006-2014); declared type INT dispatches to Number, not Year fuzzer.
Package_Version / Applications are TEXT holding dotted version strings ('5.0.0.808'); String fuzzer treats as generic text.
stock has composite PK (Shop_ID, Device_ID) and two FKs to shop and device; both parents exist and are unique.
stock.Device_ID has only 2 distinct values (4,6) over 8 rows — heavy duplication in FK child column.
stock.Shop_ID distinct=6 but samples show 9 — FK values may reference shop rows; parent shop has 12 rows.
No NOT NULL constraints anywhere; all columns nullable, so TS NULL injection is unconstrained by schema.
No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE indexes beyond PKs; drop_unique_duplicates only affects PK columns.
No self-references, no dangling FKs, no views/triggers; DDL is plain CREATE TABLE only.
All storage classes match declared types (INT->integer, TEXT->text); no affinity contradictions.
operator_ts_expectations: Device_ID / Shop_ID / Open_Year / Quantity -> Number fuzzer: uniform ints in [-10^scale,10^scale] with +-1/+-2 perturbation; scale from INT args (none) so default range.

Device, Carrier, Shop_Name, Location, Package_Version, Applications, Software_Platform, Open_Date -> String fuzzer: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0-20, plus 5 original samples, plus contaminate suffix/prefix.
Open_Date will be filled with random strings, not 'D Month' format -> queries filtering on month names or LIKE '%January%' will miss (FN).
Package_Version / Applications will be random strings, not dotted versions -> version-comparison queries (e.g. LIKE '5.0.%') miss (FN).
Number fuzzer on Open_Year produces values far outside 2006-2014 -> year-range predicates (BETWEEN 2010 AND 2015) may match spuriously (FP) or miss (FN).
stock FK columns draw from parent's final filtered values with replacement; with tiny parents (6,12 rows) and stock size possibly >parent, duplicates and NULLs (empty parent) appear.
Composite PK (Shop_ID,Device_ID) dedup keeps first occurrence; with only 2 distinct Device_ID values, many stock rows dropped -> small stock tables.
String fuzzer's 5 original samples per column preserve some real values (e.g. 'Android','iOS','Verizon Wireless') -> equality queries on those may still hit.
Number fuzzer on Device_ID/Shop_ID may produce values not in parent -> FK consistency only enforced via fill_foreign_keys_consistently, not for non-FK PK columns.
No NOT NULL/CHECK -> TS inserts all rows; rows_failed only from PK/unique collisions after dedup (rare).
Tiny DB: choose_table_sizes gives 1-31 rows per table (level 0 = 1+30u), so instances are small; joins on stock may be empty often.
String fuzzer contaminate (drop first/last char, add 5 chars) breaks exact-match queries on Device/Carrier names -> FN on equality predicates.
